name: Freakwater
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Two Louisville punks singing in a basement, harmonies that are unconventional on purpose, and more than thirty years of the darkest country songs anybody's sung with a straight face.

eras.title: Mojo Wishbean and Trippy Squashblossom
eras.text: Janet Beveridge Bean and Catherine Irwin came out of Louisville's punk scene and started singing old-time country together as a joke that stuck. Bean was already drumming in Chicago's Eleventh Dream Day; Freakwater was the thing she did on the side, and it would outlast plenty of bands that did it full time.

years.h: Janet Bean and Catherine Irwin sing in a Kentucky basement
years.p: Bloodshot Records dates Freakwater to 1985, when Janet Beveridge Bean and Catherine Irwin started recording harmonies in Bean's parents' basement in Kentucky.

q: establishing our early desire to do the wrong thing
years.h: A punk Woody Guthrie cover, on dulcimer, under fake names
years.p: On the 1987 WNUR compilation Hog Butcher to the World, Bean and Irwin play a dulcimer-driven punk take on a [[Woody Guthrie|cbd827e1-4e38-427e-a436-642683433732]] song as Mojo Wishbean and Trippy Squashblossom.
years.xp: WNUR is Northwestern University's radio station. Bean has said the track established the duo's early instinct for doing the wrong thing.

years.p: Freakwater's first album comes out on Amoeba Records, the same small label that put out Eleventh Dream Day's first records.

years.h: Dave Gay signs on as the permanent bassist
years.p: The debut LP leads Janet Bean and Catherine Irwin to David Wayne Gay, formerly of Stump the Host. He becomes Freakwater's bassist for good.

years.h: Freakwater cover Black Sabbath's War Pigs
years.p: Freakwater's first single pairs Your Goddamned Mouth with a cover of [[Black Sabbath|5182c1d9-c7d2-4dad-afa0-ccfeada921a8]]'s War Pigs, on the tiny 1 1/4 York Records.
Freakwater's second album, on Amoeba. Thrill Jockey reissued it in 1997.

eras.title: Honky-tonk for the indie kids
eras.text: Freakwater signed to Thrill Jockey, a young Chicago label, and made four albums there in six years. The harmonies drew Carter Family comparisons, the songs were full of loss and hardship, and the band showed no interest in cashing in on the reviews.

years.h: Feels Like the Third Time · Thrill Jockey
years.p: Freakwater's first album for Thrill Jockey (with City Slang in Europe). It came with a single pairing My Old Drunk Friend and Kentucky.

years.h: Freakwater join a Carter Family tribute
years.p: Freakwater appear on Amoeba's Keep on the Sunny Side: A Tribute to the Carter Family, fitting, since critics had been comparing Bean and Irwin to [[The Carter Family|29c5b1fb-5dcc-4499-b225-4ceeeb8a73d1]] from the start.

years.h: Freakwater turn up in the road movie Half-Cocked
years.p: Freakwater appear in Half-Cocked, the 1994 indie road movie.
Freakwater's third album. A single followed pairing South of Cincinnati with Cut Me Out.
years.xp: Writing about it later in Paste, Hilary Saunders heard the jauntiness of barn dances in Old Paint, but said Irwin's and Bean's voices, in their different ranges, told country stories that still sounded ahead of their time.

years.p: Freakwater's second Thrill Jockey album of the late '90s, released on LP and CD.
Freakwater close out the decade with End Time and a single pairing Hellbound with Lorraine.

eras.title: Solo detours, then Chicago
eras.text: After End Time Bean and Irwin went their own ways for a few years, and Thrill Jockey put out both of their solo records. Then Irwin left Louisville for Chicago to be closer to Bean, and Freakwater came back with a bigger band.

years.h: Catherine Irwin and Janet Bean make solo records
years.p: Catherine Irwin releases Cut Yourself a Switch and Janet Beveridge Bean releases Dragging Wonder Lake, both on Thrill Jockey. The label called them natural extensions of Freakwater.

q: you can play it into your 80's; you just play it a little slower.
years.p: After a six-year break, Catherine Irwin moves from Louisville to Chicago and Freakwater record with labelmates [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]], produced by [[Tim Rutili|8763bab7-fbfa-41ae-90d4-e5fdbb1ad63c]] at Clava Studios.
years.xp: Califone's Joe Adamik, Ben Massarella and Jim Becker played on it, along with Jacob Smith and [[James Elkington|0b4020a0-0126-4574-bbed-d9109ed60b8a]]. Freakwater toured with Califone members that year. It would be their last album for eleven years.

eras.title: Twenty years later
eras.text: A reissue brought Freakwater back. Bean and Irwin toured an old record, found a new label in Chicago's Bloodshot Records, and started a side band with two Mekons to sing about coal.

years.p: A 20-year reissue of Feels Like the Third Time gets Janet Bean and Catherine Irwin working together as Freakwater again after a break that began in 2006.

years.h: The Freakons: Freakwater and the Mekons sing about coal
years.p: Bean and Irwin join [[Jon Langford|df3f656e-5083-40a1-8e51-d111b3d65992]] and [[Sally Timms|41397aa6-1f3e-4a95-b3a6-6649bdbdbf2a]] of the [[Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]] as the Freakons, singing mining songs from Appalachia, England and Wales to raise money for Kentuckians for the Commonwealth.
years.xp: The Freakons played Hardly Strictly Bluegrass in San Francisco and the Hideout in Chicago in 2013, then again in September 2017 with violinists Jean Cook and Anna Krippenstapel, and in July 2021.

years.h: Freakwater tour Feels Like the Third Time as the main set
years.p: Freakwater go back on the road in 2014 and play the reissued Feels Like the Third Time as the core of the show.
Freakwater's first full-length in over a decade comes out on Bloodshot, preceded by a 2015 single pairing The Asp & the Albatross with Fullerene.
years.xp: Bloodshot's bio, written around the release, leans into the band's contrariness: in Bean's words, Freakwater's lack of normal ambition and inability to capitalize on acclaim is what endeared them to their most loyal fans.

years.p: Fluff & Gravy releases Freakons, recorded at the September 2017 Hideout shows by Freakwater's Bean and Irwin with Jon Langford and Sally Timms.
